newsitem.title: CHINA: China capital shuts 20 interfering pager stations.
newsitem.headline: China capital shuts 20 interfering pager stations.

text.p: China's capital Beijing has shut down 20 local pager stations after finding their signals were interfering with communications of the city's main airport, the Beijing Youth Daily said on Monday.
The pager stations, located on a hill near a remote control tower of Beijing's Capital Airport, had seriously disrupted the communications signals of the tower, the newspaper said.
The stations, many of which had been set up without official permission, had interfered with four of the main channels used by northern China air traffic authorities, it said.
"The transmitting equipment of the pager stations... have all been torn down and the problem of interference in air communications caused by the stations has been solved," it said.
The number of pagers in China's major cities has exploded in recent years, with 40 million in use nationwide by last November and millions more added each month.

Many paging companies across China have made illegal use of radio frequencies, sometimes causing interference in airline communications and prompting authorities to pledge a crack down on such networks.
